sense.text:

precepts.why:
“The secret things belong unto the Lord our God: but those things which are revealed belong unto us and to our children for ever, that we may do all the words of this law.”

“That he may run that readeth it.” The vision was written down so it could be read, and the running is shown in Amos 8.

precepts.why: Read for the word tables: “Now go, write it before them in a table, and note it in a book, that it may be for the time to come for ever and ever”. sense.text:
UFOs are called several things in the Bible. Write this down: they are called chariots, they are called clouds, they are called star. They’re mentioned throughout the Bible, and here is an example from the time of Moses.

“And they took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.” The Israelites took their journey from Succoth.

“And the Lord went before them by day in a pillar of a cloud, to lead them the way; and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light; to go by day and night: He took not away the pillar of the cloud by day, nor the pillar of fire by night, from before the people.”

These things that we read about were chariots. They don’t show you that on television, but we show it to you in the Bible.

“And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north”. Whirlwind is another name for chariots as well, and so is wheels; put those down with chariots, clouds and star.

“A great cloud, and a fire infolding itself”. They come out of the clouds, and that’s why the Most High makes mention of them being as clouds. “And a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber”: out of the midst of the fire.

“Also out of the midst thereof came the likeness of four living creatures. And this was their appearance; they had the likeness of a man.” “And every one had four faces, and every one had four wings.” They all had four faces.

“And their feet were straight feet; and the sole of their feet was like the sole of a calf’s foot”. You ever see a calf’s foot? It is split like that, like those ninja shoes they call tabi boots, split over the big toe, but hard.

“And they sparkled like the colour of burnished brass”: that’s how you know they’re black.

“Their wings were joined one to another; they turned not when they went”. Because they had four faces they didn’t have to turn to the left or to the right. If they wanted to go to the left, the face on the left side guided them; to the right, the face on the right side guided them; to go back, there was the face of an eagle in the back.

“They four had the face of a man”: each of them had the face of a man, “and the face of a lion, on the right side: and they four had the face of an ox on the left side; they four also had the face of an eagle”, the face of an eagle on the back side.

“Thus were their faces: and their wings were stretched upward; two wings of every one were joined one to another, and two covered their bodies.” It’s hard to even imagine this. If you saw this you would give up the ghost, just collapse: what the hell.
“Whither the spirit was to go, they went”: wherever the spirit that was in them went, that’s where they went.
These living creatures are angels. “Their appearance was like burning coals of fire”: black. “And out of the fire went forth lightning.”
“And the living creatures ran and returned as the appearance of a flash of lightning.” That’s how fast these creatures moved, like a flash of lightning.

precepts.why:
Ezekiel goes on in chapter 10. “And there appeared in the cherubims the form of a man’s hand under their wings.” The cherubims are another group of angels.

“Behold the four wheels by the cherubims”: there’s that term wheels, the four wheels by the cherubims, by the angels. “One wheel by one cherub, and another wheel by another cherub”: each cherub had a wheel beside it. “And the appearance of the wheels was as the colour of a beryl stone”, a green stone. “As if a wheel had been in the midst of a wheel.”

“They turned not as they went”: they did not turn as they went, “but to the place whither the head looked they followed it”, whichever way the head looked.

“And their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about, even the wheels that they four had.” Just eyes. That’s what you people think, that you can hide your sin from God. You cannot hide. How you going to hide from that? Eyes everywhere: I see you.

sense.text:

“When they saw the star, they rejoiced with exceeding great joy.” Why? Because that star led them. That’s the chariot, and they followed it.

“And was there until the death of Herod”. Thank God.

“And slew all the children that were in Bethlehem, and in all the coasts thereof, from two years old and under”. Why from two years old and under? That is why verse 11 says “they saw the young child with Mary his mother.” He was about two years old at this time. He was not a baby in swaddling clothes; he was at the age they call the terrible twos, mine, mine, mine.

precepts.why:
Who were these wise men from the east? “And there were dwelling at Jerusalem Jews, devout men, out of every nation under heaven.” Every man heard them speak in his own language, “wherein we were born”.

These chariots are not leaving. “And shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof.” Remember the argument: one group of Christians says it’s a biscuit flying through the sky, another group says it’s a piece of paper. Now what biscuit or what piece of paper can consume timber and consume stones? This is a chariot. Don’t let these Christian idiots ever, ever fool y’all.

Read it again with 2 Thessalonians 2 and it goes right along: “I will bring it forth”, the Most High is going to bring the chariots forth, because the prophets are going to speak it and cause them to be activated. “It shall enter into the house of the thief”: the chariots are going to enter into all those that oppressed us around the world. “Him that sweareth falsely by my name”: they blasphemed against the Israelites, they blasphemed against his Bible, and they’re going to pay for that. “It shall remain in the midst of his house”: they can’t get rid of it; they’re trying to stop it and they can’t stop it. “And shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof”: the Most High is going to destroy it all, burn it up, so it’s going to be totally liquefied. Why? Because the Most High is causing the prophets to bring it out, and the angels are activated to do just that.

That’s some powerful stuff: there’s going to be a time you’re going to be able to call the chariot, and it’s going to be right there.

“See what is this that goeth forth.” An ephah is not the ephod; those are two different things. An ephah is an ancient Hebrew unit of dry measure, equal to about a bushel. So it was a basket of sorts that held a certain amount of measurement.
“This is an ephah that goeth forth”: now he’s seeing something different. “This is their resemblance through all the earth.”

“And, behold, there was lifted up a talent of lead: and this is a woman that sitteth in the midst of the ephah.” Now he sees a woman in the midst of the ephah, that measurement; there’s a woman sitting in there. That woman represents sinful Israel.
“And he said, This is wickedness.” “And he cast the weight of lead upon the mouth thereof”: the angel cast lead on top of the ephah to lock it in for this judgment, for us.

“Behold, there came out two women”: now he sees two women. “And the wind was in their wings; for they had wings like the wings of a stork: and they lifted up the ephah between the earth and the heaven.” They lifted up this ephah between heaven and earth.
“Whither do these bear the ephah?” Where are they taking the ephah with sinful Israel?

“To build it an house in the land of Shinar”: Shinar is Babylon, Babylon the great. Old Babylon was destroyed already, and this is the Persian captivity, so this Babylon is the future Babylon, which we are in right now. “And it shall be established, and set there upon her own base.” The angel is letting Zechariah know that Israel is going to be established in Babylon.

precepts.why:
“For the mystery of iniquity doth already work: only he who now letteth will let, until he be taken out of the way.” “And then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth”.

That’s the reason why they don’t want us teaching: as we teach, those angels are being activated. Every time this Bible comes out and they try to hide it, the Most High is going to make them deal with it. The Most High is causing this word; when we speak, we speak the words of the Most High, and the angels are activated.

“Whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth”: that’s what we were reading in Zechariah, “shall consume it with the timber thereof and the stones thereof.” The Lord consumes with the spirit of the Bible spoken by the prophets. “And shall destroy with the brightness of his coming”: he shall destroy them with the brightness of the chariots. That’s exactly why what we read here goes along with what we read in Zechariah 5:4.
What does the woman in the ephah represent? “How is the faithful city become an harlot!” That’s talking about us. “It was full of judgment; righteousness lodged in it; but now murderers.”

“I have likened the daughter of Zion to a comely and delicate woman.” There’s the woman. So when you go back to Zechariah 5:7, “this is a woman that sitteth in the midst of the ephah”: that woman represents sinful Israel, and the angel calls her “wickedness”.

“Be in pain, and labour to bring forth”: the Lord don’t care about your battle fatigue. Everybody’s tired, we’re trying to get out of captivity, and he says be in pain and labour to bring forth. “O daughter of Zion”: that’s a message to us. “Like a woman in travail”: work like a woman in travail.

“For now shalt thou go forth out of the city”: we left out of the city of Israel. “And thou shalt dwell in the field, and thou shalt go even to Babylon”. That’s the same thing the angel told Zechariah: the ephah with the woman is carried to build it an house in the land of Shinar, Babylon.

“There shalt thou be delivered”: we’re going to be delivered from this place here.

sense.text:
“A woman clothed with the sun, and the moon under her feet”: the sun and the moon represent God’s law, so we have the law. “And upon her head a crown of twelve stars”: that crown of twelve stars represents the twelve tribes of Israel. That’s the evidence it ain’t talking about all nations; it’s talking about the Israelites, the twelve tribes.

You cannot get around the twelve tribes. Understanding who the twelve tribes are will help you understand the Bible, but once you’re confused and think the Israelites are those white people over there, you’re lost already. That’s why these black Christians don’t know a dag gone thing: all they know is the white man: they love him more than their own mom and daddy, ‘I just love Jesus.’
“And she being with child cried, travailing in birth”: Israel being with child.

“Behold a great red dragon”: this great red dragon represents Esau, our brother Esau, Edom. “Having seven heads”: Greece, Rome, Spain, France, Germany, Russia, Great Britain, and the eighth was America. “And ten horns”: Belgium, Luxembourg, Netherlands, Germany, United Kingdom, Italy, Greece, France, Denmark and Ireland. This is the European Empire.

“And his tail drew the third part of the stars of heaven”: the tail there is referring to Rome. Out of twelve stars he took down four: Judah, Benjamin, Levi, and the fourth was a mixture of the northern kingdom. Write that down.

“And the dragon stood before the woman”: the dragon stood before the Israelites. “For to devour her child as soon as it was born”: to kill Christ as soon as he was born. The Lord is calling the white man here the devil; he’s calling him the great red dragon.

“And she brought forth a man child”: that’s Christ, “who was to rule all nations with a rod of iron”. This is why you know the wise men were Israelites. Herod knew the prophecy that Christ was coming to destroy the nations, so why would those wise men be men of other races coming to worship the king? Those were Israelites.

“And her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne”: we just read that in Acts 1:9.

“And the woman fled into the wilderness”: that wilderness is Africa. 70 AD came and we fled into the wilderness of Africa. “Where she hath a place prepared of God”: from there we had a place prepared of God in the Americas. “That they should feed her there”.

precepts.why:
What do the sun and the moon represent? “For the commandment is a lamp; and the law is light”. The law is light. “And reproofs of instruction are the way of life”.

So the sun and the moon the woman is clothed with represent God’s law.
Why does it say great red dragon? “And the first came out red, all over like an hairy garment; and they called his name Esau.” So this great red dragon represents Esau.
Job said, “I am a brother to dragons”. So that great red dragon was our brother: Esau, Edom.

In case you doubt that’s the proper breakdown, here’s the precept. “Behold, the angel of the Lord appeareth to Joseph in a dream, saying, Arise, and take the young child and his mother, and flee into Egypt”: flee into Africa. “And be thou there until I bring thee word”. Why? “For Herod will seek the young child to destroy him”.

Look up Herod: the Herods were Idumean rulers of Palestine. And Idumea means pertaining to Edom; it is the Greek and Roman name for Edom. So Herod was an Edomite. Herod was red and hairy all over like a hairy garment. That’s the dragon standing before the woman “for to devour her child as soon as it was born”: to kill Christ as soon as he was born.
“Her child was caught up unto God, and to his throne”: “And when he had spoken these things, while they beheld, he was taken up; and a cloud received him out of their sight.”

Jump down to verse 14 and he repeats what we just read in verse 6. “And to the woman were given two wings of a great eagle”: a way to escape. “That she might fly into the wilderness”: that’s Africa. “Into her place”: that’s Babylon, the United States of America.

“Where she is nourished for a time, and times, and half a time”: 350 years. “From the face of the serpent”: so we’re nourished by the devil here. We are nourished by Satan. This is what the Bible says.

sense.text:
“And their dead bodies shall lie in the street of the great city”: Proverbs and Isaiah show why we’re dead. “Which spiritually is called Sodom and Egypt”: this ain’t the literal Sodom or the literal Egypt; it’s a spiritual Sodom, a spiritual Egypt.

“Where also our Lord was crucified”: his image and his teachings were crucified here. This ain’t the real Jerusalem, but it is a spiritual Jerusalem, because they crucified Christ’s image here and crucified his teachings with those damnable images, those abominations. They come with that peace and love and then put you to death right behind that image.

“Shall see their dead bodies three days and an half”: 350 years. “And shall not suffer their dead bodies to be put in graves”, because we’re not physically dead. We’re spiritually dead as a race, but we’re not physically dead.

“And they that dwell upon the earth shall rejoice over them, and make merry”: that’s your Christmas right there. Make merry means Merry Christmas. “And shall send gifts one to another”: they gave us away as gifts. If you don’t believe it, there was a movie, Birth of a Nation, where a woman’s birthday or some holiday was coming up, and one turned and said to the master, why don’t you get that female slave for Miss such and such, and he got her as a gift for his sister. We were the gifts. Our sons and our daughters were the gifts: you had kids, and they took your kids from you and gave them as a gift on Christmas to somebody else.

“Because these two prophets tormented them that dwelt on the earth”: these two prophets start with Moses and Elijah, but it goes to the remnant of Israel, meaning Judah and Israel. Write that down.

“The Spirit of life from God entered into them”: that’s the Holy Ghost. The proof that we’re waking up is the proof we have the Holy Ghost on us. It might be at a low level, but we got it. “And they stood upon their feet”: we’re standing up now, standing on our feet.

“And great fear fell upon them which saw them”: the nations are mad. God’s people are waking up again, and this is what makes all the nations mad. They know that when we come out, we are connected with those chariots. They know what’s coming. When they see that, they say these are the guys we’ve been reading about in that Bible: we got a problem over here.

“And they heard a great voice from heaven saying unto them, Come up hither. And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud”: in a cloud, that’s a chariot. “And their enemies beheld them.”

You’ve got people that read this and still say they don’t believe it; we can’t help you. Back in the late ’90s there was a meeting in Chicago, and a lot of so-called black Israelite leaders were there trying to buy an airplane. Asked what the airplane was for, they said, so that we can escape the destruction. Looking around the auditorium: not trying to be a wise ass, but all of us cannot fit on one plane. They cursed him out.

“And the same hour was there a great earthquake, and the tenth part of the city fell”: the tenth part of the city is going to fall. “And the remnant were affrighted”: we’re going to be scared, because we’re going to watch the destruction of millions and millions and millions of people. “And gave glory to the God of heaven.”

precepts.why: Why are we dead? “The man that wandereth out of the way of understanding shall remain in the congregation of the dead.” Wander out of the way of understanding and you remain in the congregation of the dead. That’s why it says “their dead bodies”.

“Therefore is judgment far from us, neither doth justice overtake us”: that’s why we’re waiting for justice. Here in this country, or any country, we never receive true justice. “We wait for light, but behold obscurity”: confusion. “For brightness, but we walk in darkness.”

“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes”: like blind people. “We stumble at noonday as in the night”: the sun’s fully out and we’re stumbling at noonday. “We are in desolate places as dead men.” God says we are as dead men: the walking dead. That’s the burlap over their eyes, sitting up in white man Christianity churches, can’t see anything. Totally dead.

“We roar all like bears, and mourn sore like doves: we look for judgment, but there is none”: we’re always looking for judgment, but there’s no judgment for us. “For salvation, but it is far off from us”: we all want salvation, but it’s far off. Why? Because we’re in the wrong places. We’re in a white man’s church looking for salvation, in the white man’s educational system looking for justice, and it ain’t going to happen.

“For our transgressions are multiplied before thee”: our transgressions are being multiplied by us ignoring the Bible and going to what white society has to say, what Edomite customs and traditions have to say. We’re trusting that. “And our sins testify against us: for our transgressions are with us; and as for our iniquities, we know them”. So now we know why we’re dead.

“And they ascended up to heaven in a cloud”: watch this. “Then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him”: against the white man in all nations. “And made no account of his labours”: they made no account of the free slave labor we gave.

“When they see it, they shall be troubled with terrible fear”. What are they going to be afraid about? “And shall be amazed at the strangeness of his salvation”. See that part, the strangeness of his salvation: that’s what we just read in Revelation 11:12: “they ascended up to heaven in a cloud”.
“They ascended up to heaven in a cloud”, and in case you forgot what the cloud is: “who maketh the clouds his chariot: who walketh upon the wings of the wind”. The cloud is a chariot.
“Who are these that fly as a cloud, and as the doves to their windows?” That’s what it’s talking about: these that fly as a cloud are in the chariots, the clouds the Lord makes his chariot.

“Come, my people”, watch this, “enter thou into thy chambers”: that’s the chariots. “And shut thy doors about thee”: shut the doors of the chariot about you. “Hide thyself as it were for a little moment, until the indignation be overpast”: until the destruction is over.

Put your mind in the frame of what you just looked at. Just knowing that your enemies at that moment will be gone forever: imagine waking up and you got no more oppressor. It’s hard to even fathom. You won’t even know how to act; you might start break dancing and dancing the jig.

“For, behold, the Lord cometh out of his place to punish the inhabitants of the earth”: that’s what the chariots are all about. He’s coming to punish the inhabitants of the earth “for their iniquity”, for their sins. “The earth also shall disclose her blood, and shall no more cover her slain.”

“He that dwelleth in the secret place of the most High”: so brothers and sisters, we better stay in this Bible. I don’t care what you got going on in your personal life, you better stay in this book and stay connected in the brotherhood of Israel, the nation of Israel. If you leave this right here, you lost; we can’t help you. He that dwells there “shall abide under the shadow of the Almighty.”

“I will say of the Lord, He is my refuge and my fortress: my God; in him will I trust. Surely he shall deliver thee from the snare of the fowler”: the snare of the fowler is the white man in this system; God says, I’m going to deliver you from that. “And from the noisome pestilence. He shall cover thee with his feathers, and under his wings shalt thou trust: his truth shall be thy shield and buckler”: the truth in Christ shall be our shield and buckler. That’s our protection.

“Thou shalt not be afraid for the terror by night; nor for the arrow that flieth by day”: that arrow that flies by day is a missile, the ICBM, the intercontinental ballistic missile. God says don’t even fear that. “Nor for the pestilence that walketh in darkness; nor for the destruction that wasteth at noonday”: the destruction will come at noonday.

“A thousand shall fall at thy side, and ten thousand at thy right hand; but it shall not come nigh thee.” This is what Revelation 11 was saying: when we look out the windows, a thousand shall fall at your side and ten thousand at your right hand, but it shall not come nigh us. “Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold and see the reward of the wicked.” Why? “Because thou hast made the Lord, which is my refuge, even the most High, thy habitation”. “There shall no evil befall thee, neither shall any plague come nigh thy dwelling”: no plague shall come near our dwelling.

We don’t care if you don’t believe it at home; we believe the Bible. “And there shall be signs in the sun, and in the moon, and in the stars; and upon the earth distress of nations”: we’re seeing that now. “With perplexity”: confusion. “The sea and the waves roaring”: that’s the nations warring.

“Men’s hearts failing them for fear”: that’s some of those videos we saw. People are scared, they’re terrified: what does this mean, what are those UFOs? “And for looking after those things which are coming on the earth: for the powers of heaven shall be shaken.” That’s war, brothers and sisters: war in Ukraine, war in Israel, war on Palestine, war with Iran, war with Iraq.

“And then shall they see the Son of man coming in a cloud with power and great glory.” That’s what we want to see right there: the same cloud of Revelation 11:12. “And when these things begin to come to pass”, and they are coming to pass, “then look up, and lift up your heads; for your redemption draweth nigh.” Your redemption is at hand, brothers and sisters.

sense.text: “Woe to them that go down to Egypt for help”: we always want help from America. “And stay on horses, and trust in chariots, because they are many; and in horsemen, because they are very strong”: Mr. White Man, save us. “But they look not unto the Holy One of Israel”: it’s time we now start looking to the Holy One of Israel. “Neither seek the Lord”: there are people out there not seeking the Lord. Christianity does not seek the Lord; they seek the white man for help. He’s their God.

You got to understand verse two: “Yet he also is wise, and will bring evil”. Why would the Lord bring evil on him? God is saying, you’re wicked as hell, you got to go. “And will not call back his words”: he ain’t calling back his word, brothers and sisters. “But will arise against the house of the evildoers”: that’s the house of the thief. “And against the help of them that work iniquity”: if you help them work iniquity, you’re going to die too.

“Now the Egyptians are men, and not God”: the white man is human, and he is not God, brothers and sisters. “And their horses flesh, and not spirit”: their chariots are flesh, they come from the ground; they’re not spirit, because God’s chariots are spirit. “When the Lord shall stretch out his hand, both he that helpeth shall fall, and he that is holpen shall fall down, and they all shall fail together.”

precepts.why:
Apocrypha time. We don’t give a damn if you don’t believe in the Apocrypha; we believe in it here, because it was in the Bible from the beginning. The hell is wrong with you? Pay close attention, this is a prayer, the prayer for the Lord to stretch out his hand against the nations.

“Have mercy upon us, O Lord God of all, and behold us: and send thy fear upon all the nations that seek not after thee.” So the prayer is: send your fear upon all the nations that seek not after thee. “Lift up thy hand against the strange nations”: now we’re asking God to lift up his hand against those strange nations, against the white man, against China, against Japan, against Saudi Arabia. “And let them see thy power.”

“As thou wast sanctified in us before them: so be thou magnified among them before us”: just like you brought us down, Lord, bring them down. “And let them know thee, as we have known thee, that there is no God but only thou, O God.”

“Shew new signs”: now we’re asking the Lord to show new signs in the earth. “And make other strange wonders”: we’re seeing other strange wonders, are we not? Yes we are. “Glorify thy hand and thy right arm, that they may set forth thy wondrous works.”

“Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath”: God, pour your wrath on this earth. “Take away the adversary”: take away the white man and all the nations. “And destroy the enemy.” Do y’all hear what this prayer is saying? Make the time short: now we’re asking the Lord to make the time short. “Remember the covenant”: the covenant of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, “and let them declare thy wonderful works.”

“Let him that escapeth be consumed by the rage of the fire”: whoever escapes in their bunkers, let them be consumed by destruction. “And let them perish that oppress the people”: let all those nations perish that oppress the Israelites. “Smite in sunder the heads of the rulers of the heathen, that say, There is none other but we.”

“Gather all the tribes of Jacob together”: that’s our prayer, Lord, gather all the tribes of Jacob together. That’s our mission, that’s our goal. “And inherit thou them, as from the beginning”: inherit us just like you had us from the beginning; do it again, Lord. “O Lord, have mercy upon the people that is called by thy name, and upon Israel, whom thou hast named thy firstborn.”

sense.text:
Before we close out: Habakkuk chapter 3. We can’t get out of here without that chapter. “A prayer of Habakkuk the prophet upon Shigionoth. O Lord, I have heard thy speech, and was afraid”: I’ve heard what the Bible said, and I was afraid.

“O Lord, revive thy work”: we’re the work. We’re part of that work. Like Ecclesiasticus 36 said, show new signs, make other strange wonders in the earth; a part of that is us waking up. “In the midst of the years”: that’s the 350 years. “In the midst of the years make known”: that’s what you brothers are about, making known God’s works in the street; you sisters, making known God’s works to your children. “In wrath remember mercy”: in your wrath, Lord, remember mercy.
“God came from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran”: that’s over in the Middle East. “Selah” means it is true. “His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.”

“And his brightness was as the light; he had horns coming out of his hand”: when it says horns, it’s beams of power coming out of his hands. That’s the horns. “And there was the hiding of his power”: he had to hold back some of his power. That’s what the hiding of his power means.

“Before him went the pestilence, and burning coals went forth at his feet. He stood, and measured the earth”: imagine, the Lord had to measure the earth to see how much power he’s going to use to destroy the nations that come against him. “He beheld, and drove asunder the nations; and the everlasting mountains were scattered, the perpetual hills did bow: his ways are everlasting.”

“I saw the tents of Cushan in affliction”: he said, I saw Ethiopia in affliction. “And the curtains of the land of Midian”: all them in Saudi Arabia, that whole region. He said, I saw them catching hell too.

“Was the Lord displeased against the rivers?” The rivers represent nations: was the Lord displeased against the nations of people? “Was thine anger against the rivers? was thy wrath against the sea, that thou didst ride upon thine horses and thy chariots of salvation?” He rides upon his horses and his chariots of salvation.

“Thy bow was made quite naked”: his bow is talking about the Bible. It’s quite obvious God’s coming for war; nowhere does the Bible say he’s coming in peace. “According to the oaths of the tribes”: that’s the proof of what the bow is. “Even thy word”: see that right there, even thy word. That’s what the bow is talking about. “Selah”: it’s true. “Thou didst cleave the earth with rivers.”

“The mountains saw thee, and they trembled”: the mountains are the nations. The nations see Christ, and they’re going to tremble. “The overflowing of the water passed by: the deep uttered his voice”: the deep of the ocean is going to utter his voice. “And lifted up his hands on high”: tsunamis.
“The sun and moon stood still in their habitation: at the light of thine arrows they went, and at the shining of thy glittering spear”: that’s missiles going back and forth, back and forth.
“Thou didst march through the land in indignation”: you march through the land with righteous anger. “Thou didst thresh the heathen in anger”: he’s going to kill the nations in anger.

“Thou wentest forth for the salvation of thy people”: wait a minute. It didn’t say he came for the salvation of the Jehovah’s Witness or the Pentecostal. It’s thy people. “Even for salvation with thine anointed; thou woundedst the head out of the house of the wicked”: he’s going to wound America; that’s the house of the wicked. The head: he’s going to cut their head off. “By discovering the foundation unto the neck”: although the other nations fight America, the Lord said, I got to get in there; I got to finally take them out. “Selah”: it’s true.

“Thou didst strike through with his staves the head of his villages”: that’s Germany, Britain, France and so on. “They came out as a whirlwind to scatter me”: they’re coming with their jets, their planes, their missiles to scatter the Son of God. “Their rejoicing was as to devour the poor secretly”: see what God reveals. He’s revealing to us that the nations are plotting against us secretly to destroy each and every one of us.

“Thou didst walk through the sea with thine horses, through the heap of great waters. When I heard, my belly trembled”: when he read the scriptures and saw the vision, his belly trembled. “My lips quivered at the voice”: you know when your bottom lip just trembles because you’re scared as hell? That was Habakkuk. “Rottenness entered into my bones, and I trembled in myself, that I might rest in the day of trouble”: he said, Lord, when you come back I want to be dead; I want to be resting in heaven when you come back.

“When he cometh up unto the people”: when he comes up to the people, the nations of the world, he will invade them. God is going to invade this earth. So this is the real Space Invaders: when they came up with that game Space Invaders, the Most High already had it in the Bible.

precepts.why: When it says displeased against the rivers: “Woe to the multitude of many people, which make a noise like the noise of the seas; and to the rushing of nations, that make a rushing like the rushing of mighty waters!” So these rivers represent nations. The Lord’s anger against the rivers and his wrath against the sea is his anger against the nations of people.
